title.zh: 卷四百三十七 列傳第一百九十六 儒林七 程迥 劉清之 眞德秀 魏了翁 廖德明
title.en: Volume 437 Biographies 196: Confucian Scholars 7 - Cheng Jiong, Liu Qingzhi, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Leweng, Liao Deming
title.raw: 卷四百三十七 列傳第一百九十六 儒林七 程迥 劉清之 眞德秀 魏了翁 廖德明 Volume 437 Biographies 196: Confucian Scholars 7 - Cheng Jiong, Liu Qingzhi, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Leweng, Liao Deming

sentences.zh: 儒林七○程迥劉清之真德秀魏了翁廖德明

translations.literal: Confucian Scholars 7—Cheng Jiong, Liu Qingzhi, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Leweng, Liao Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars 7: Cheng Jiong, Liu Qingzhi, Zhen Dexiu, Wei Leweng, and Liao Deming

sentences.zh: 程迥，字可久，應天府寧陵人。

translations.literal: Cheng Jiong, courtesy name Kejiu, was a native of Ningling in Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiong, whose courtesy name was Kejiu, came from Ningling in Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家於沙隨，靖康之亂，徙紹興之餘姚。

translations.literal: His family dwelt at Shasui; in the disorder of the Jingkang era they moved to Yuyao in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived at Shasui, but during the upheaval of the Jingkang era they relocated to Yuyao in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 年十五，丁內外艱，孤貧飄泊，無以自振。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he suffered the loss of both parents, and orphaned, poor, and adrift, he had no means to lift himself up.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he lost both parents and was left orphaned, destitute, and adrift, with no way to recover his footing.

sentences.zh: 二十餘，始知讀書，時亂甫定，西北士大夫多在錢塘，迥得以考德問業焉。

translations.literal: Past twenty he first came to study books; the turmoil had just settled, and scholar-officials from the northwest were mostly at Qiantang, so Jiong was able to examine virtue and inquire into learning there.
translations.idiomatic: Not until he was past twenty did he begin to study. The realm had only just settled after the chaos, and many scholar-officials from the northwest had gathered at Qiantang, where Jiong was able to seek out teachers and pursue his studies.

sentences.zh: 登隆興元年進士第，曆揚州泰興尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Longxing and successively served as marshal of Taixing in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Longxing era (1163) and served as marshal of Taixing in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 訓武郎楊大烈有田十頃，死而妻女存。

translations.literal: Training Martial Gentleman Yang Dalie had ten qing of land; he died, leaving his wife and daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dalie, a Training Martial Gentleman, owned ten qing of land. After his death his wife and daughter remained.

sentences.zh: 俄有訟其妻非正室者，官沒其貲，且追十年所入租。

translations.literal: Soon someone sued alleging that his wife was not the principal consort; the authorities confiscated the property and moreover sought ten years of rent already collected.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone sued, claiming the wife was not the lawful principal consort. The authorities confiscated the estate and demanded repayment of ten years' rent.

sentences.zh: 部使者以諉迥，迥曰：“大烈死，貲產當歸其女。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner shifted the blame onto Jiong; Jiong said, "When Dalie died, the property ought to go to his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner put the case on Jiong, who replied, "When Dalie died, his property should have passed to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 女死，當歸所生母可也。

translations.literal: When the daughter dies, it should return to the mother who bore her—that is sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: If the daughter had died, it would rightly have gone to her birth mother."

sentences.zh: 調饒州德興丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Dexing in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Dexing in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 盜入縣民齊匊家，平素所不快者，皆罥絓逮獄。

translations.literal: Thieves entered the home of a county resident named Qi Ju, and all whom Ju had long disliked were implicated and thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves broke into the home of a county resident named Qi Ju, everyone Ju had long resented was implicated and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 州屬迥決禁囚，辨其冤者縱遣之。

translations.literal: The prefecture assigned Jiong to decide cases of prisoners in custody; those he found innocent he released.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture assigned Jiong to review prisoners in custody, and he released those he found innocent.

sentences.zh: 匊訟不已。

translations.literal: Ju sued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Ju kept filing suit without end.

sentences.zh: 會獲盜寧國，匊猶訟還所縱之人，迥曰：“盜既獲矣，再令追捕，或死於道路，使其骨肉何依，豈審冤之道哉！

translations.literal: When the thieves were captured in Ningguo, Ju still sued to have those who had been released brought back; Jiong said, "The thieves are already captured—if we order pursuit again, some may die on the road; what will their kin rely on? Is this the way to discern wrongful conviction?
translations.idiomatic: When the thieves were captured in Ningguo, Ju still demanded that those Jiong had released be rearrested. Jiong said, "The thieves are already in custody. To hunt down the men I released again risks their dying on the road—what would become of their families? Is that how one clears the wrongly accused?

sentences.zh: ”唐肅宗時，縣有程氏女，其父兄為盜所殺，因掠女去，隱忍十餘年，手刃盡誅其黨，刳其肝心以祭其父兄。

translations.literal: " In the time of Emperor Suzong of Tang, there was a woman of the Cheng clan in the county whose father and elder brothers were killed by bandits and who was carried off with them; she endured in concealment for more than ten years, then with her own hand slew and exterminated the whole band, gouging out their livers and hearts to sacrifice to her father and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: " In the reign of Emperor Suzong of Tang, a woman of the Cheng clan in the county had seen her father and brothers killed by bandits who carried her off. She bore it in silence for more than ten years, then with her own hand killed every member of the band, cutting out their livers and hearts to offer to her father and brothers.

sentences.zh: 迥取《春秋》復仇之義，頌之曰：“大而得其正者也。

translations.literal: Jiong took the principle of vengeance in the Spring and Autumn Annals and praised her, saying, "Great, yet attaining what is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong invoked the Spring and Autumn Annals' doctrine of vengeance and composed a eulogy calling her "great in scale yet true to what is right."

sentences.zh: ”表之曰“英孝程烈女”。

translations.literal: " He memorialized her as "Heroic and Filial, the Stern Woman of the Cheng Clan."
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted a memorial honoring her as the "Heroic and Filial Stern Woman of the Cheng Clan."

sentences.zh: 改知隆興府進賢縣。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as magistrate of Jinxian in Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Jinxian in Longxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 省符下，知平江府王佐決陳長年輒私賣田，其從子訴有司十有八年，母魚氏年七十坐獄。

translations.literal: A provincial order came down: Wang Zuo, prefect of Pingjiang, had ruled that Chen Changnian had rashly sold land in private; his nephew had sued before the authorities for eighteen years, and the mother, Lady Yu, aged seventy, sat in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial directive arrived: Wang Zuo, prefect of Pingjiang, had ruled that Chen Changnian had sold family land on his own authority. The nephew had been suing before the authorities for eighteen years, and the mother, Lady Yu, now seventy, sat in prison.

sentences.zh: 廷辨按法追正，令候母死服闋日，理為己分，令天下郡縣視此為法。

translations.literal: The court deliberation, applying the law to rectify the matter, ordered that one wait until the day when mourning for the mother was completed after her death, then settle what was one's proper share, and commanded all commanderies and counties under Heaven to take this as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: After court deliberation the ruling was corrected by law: the nephew was to wait until mourning for his mother was complete after her death, then receive his proper share. All commanderies and counties were ordered to follow this precedent.

sentences.zh: 迥為議曰：“天下之人孰無母慈？

translations.literal: Jiong submitted a deliberation, saying, "Who under Heaven is without a mother's kindness?
translations.idiomatic: Jiong submitted a memorial arguing, "Who under Heaven lacks a mother's love?

sentences.zh: 子若孫宜定省溫凊，不宜有私財也。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons ought to attend to her comfort morning and evening and warm her in cold and cool her in heat; they ought not to hold private property.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons ought to attend her morning and evening and see to her comfort in cold and heat; they ought not to hold private property.

sentences.zh: 在律，別籍者有禁，異財者有禁。

translations.literal: In the statutes, establishing separate household registers is forbidden, and holding separate property is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes forbid establishing separate household registers and forbid holding property apart from the family estate.

sentences.zh: 當報牒之初，縣令杖而遣之，使聽命於其母可矣，何稽滯遍訴有司，而達於登聞院乎？

translations.literal: At the first report, the county magistrate should have beaten him with the staff and sent him off, letting him obey his mother's command—that would have sufficed. Why drag the case through every office for so long until it reached the Court of Memorials?
translations.idiomatic: When the case was first reported, the county magistrate should simply have beaten the nephew with the staff and sent him home to obey his mother. Why let the suit drag through every office for eighteen years until it reached the Court of Memorials?

sentences.zh: 《春秋穀梁傳》注曰：‘臣無訟君之道’，為衛侯鄭與元咺發論也。

translations.literal: The commentary on the Guliang Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'A subject has no way to sue his lord'—this argument was raised concerning Marquis Zheng of Wei and Yuan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on the Guliang Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says, "A subject has no right to sue his lord"—an argument raised in the case of Marquis Zheng of Wei and Yuan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 夫諸侯之於命大夫猶若此，子孫之於母乃使坐獄以對吏，愛其親者聞之，不覺泣涕之橫集也。

translations.literal: If even for feudal lords toward appointed grandees it is thus, yet for sons and grandsons toward a mother to make her sit in prison to answer before clerks—those who love their kin, hearing of it, cannot keep tears from flooding forth.
translations.idiomatic: If even a feudal lord may not be sued by his grandee, how much worse to make a mother sit in prison answering before clerks because her son and grandson sued one another. Anyone who loves his parents, hearing of this, cannot keep the tears from streaming down.

sentences.zh: 按令文：分財產，謂祖父母、父母服闋已前所有者。

translations.literal: According to the ordinance text: dividing property refers to what grandparents and parents owned before mourning was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinances state that dividing property applies only to what grandparents and parents owned before the mourning period was complete.

sentences.zh: 然則母在，子孫不得有私財。

translations.literal: Thus, while the mother lives, sons and grandsons may not have private property.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, while the mother lives, sons and grandsons may not hold private property.

sentences.zh: 借使其母一朝盡費，其子孫亦不得違教令也。

translations.literal: Even supposing the mother spent it all in a single morning, her sons and grandsons still could not disobey her command.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the mother spent the entire estate in a single morning, her sons and grandsons still could not defy her authority.

sentences.zh: 既使歸於其母，其日前所費，乃卑幼輒用尊長物，法須五年尊長告乃為理。

translations.literal: Since it is made to return to the mother, what was spent before was juniors rashly using the property of seniors; by law one must wait five years until the senior reports it before a claim may be heard.
translations.idiomatic: If the property is returned to the mother, what was spent earlier amounts to juniors using a senior's property without permission; by law a claim may be heard only after five years and only if the senior files it.

sentences.zh: 何至豫期母死，又開他日爭訟之端也？

translations.literal: Why go so far as to anticipate the mother's death in advance and open the door to future litigation?
translations.idiomatic: Why anticipate the mother's death in advance and open the door to future lawsuits?

sentences.zh: 抑亦安知不令之子孫不死於母之前乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, who can know that an unfilial son or grandson will not die before the mother?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, who can guarantee that an unfilial son or grandson will not die before his mother?

sentences.zh: 守令者，民之師帥，政教之所由出。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are the teachers and commanders of the people; from them government and instruction proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are the teachers and leaders of the people; from them government and moral instruction proceed.

sentences.zh: 誠宜正守令不職之愆與子孫不孝之罪，以敬天下之為人母者。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to correct the fault of prefects and magistrates who fail in duty and the crime of unfilial sons and grandsons, so as to show respect to all who are mothers under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to punish negligent prefects and magistrates and unfilial sons and grandsons alike, so as to show due respect to every mother under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 民饑，府檄有訴閉糴及糶與商賈者，迥即論報之曰：“力田之人，細米每鬥才九十五文，逼於稅賦，是以出糶，非上戶也。

translations.literal: The people were famished; the prefecture issued orders citing complaints of hoarding grain and of selling grain to merchants; Jiong at once submitted a reasoned reply, saying, "Those who work the fields—fine rice is only ninety-five cash per dou; pressed by taxes and levies, they therefore sell grain out; they are not wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine the prefecture issued orders citing complaints of grain hoarding and of selling grain to merchants. Jiong replied at once: "Farmers sell fine rice for only ninety-five cash per dou, driven by tax burdens—not wealthy households hoarding grain.

sentences.zh: 縣境不出貨寶，苟不與外人交易，輸官之錢何由而得？

translations.literal: Within the county boundaries no precious goods are produced; if one does not trade with outsiders, whence can the money paid to the government be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Our county produces no luxury goods. If farmers cannot trade with outsiders, how will they obtain the cash to pay their taxes?

sentences.zh: 今強者群聚，脅持取錢，毆傷人者甚眾，民不敢入市，坐致缺食。

translations.literal: Now the strong gather in groups, extort money by intimidation, and beat and injure many; the people dare not enter the markets, and thus sit by while food grows scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Now bullies gather in gangs, extort money by force, and beat many people. The people dare not enter the markets, and food grows scarce as a result.

sentences.zh: ”申論再三，見從乃已。

translations.literal: " He argued repeatedly; only when his view was accepted did the orders cease.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued his case repeatedly, and the orders were withdrawn only when his view prevailed.

sentences.zh: 縣大水，亡稻麥，郡蠲租稅至薄，迥白於府曰：“是驅民流徙耳！

translations.literal: Great flood in the county destroyed the rice and wheat; the prefecture remitted taxes only slightly; Jiong reported to the prefecture, saying, "This will only drive the people to wander in exile!
translations.idiomatic: A great flood destroyed the county's rice and wheat crops. The prefecture offered only a slight tax remission. Jiong reported to the prefecture, "This will only drive the people into exile!

sentences.zh: 賦不可得，徒存欠籍。

translations.literal: The levies cannot be collected, yet empty arrears records alone remain.
translations.idiomatic: No revenue can be collected, yet empty records of arrears will remain on the books.

sentences.zh: ”乃悉蠲之。

translations.literal: " He then remitted them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: " He then remitted the taxes entirely.

sentences.zh: 郡僚猶曰：“度江後來，未嚐全放，恐戶部不從。

translations.literal: Prefectural colleagues still said, "Since crossing the Yangzi in the southward retreat, we have never remitted everything; I fear the Ministry of Revenue will not consent."
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues at the prefecture still objected, "Since the court crossed the Yangzi, we have never granted a full remission—the Ministry of Revenue may not approve."

sentences.zh: ”迥力論之曰：“唐人損七，則租、庸、調俱免。

translations.literal: " Jiong argued forcefully, saying, "Under the Tang, when the loss was seven-tenths, rent, corvée, and the equalization levy were all exempted.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong argued forcefully: "Under the Tang, when crop loss reached seven-tenths, rent, corvée, and the equalization levy were all waived.

sentences.zh: 今損十矣。

translations.literal: Now the loss is complete—ten-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Here the loss is total—ten-tenths.

sentences.zh: 夏稅、役錢不免，是猶用其二也，不可謂寬。

translations.literal: Yet summer tax and service money are not exempted—this is still taking two parts; it cannot be called lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet summer tax and service levies remain—this still collects two parts of what cannot be paid. That cannot be called relief.

sentences.zh: ”議乃息。

translations.literal: " The debate then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " The debate then ended.

sentences.zh: 境內有婦人傭身紡績舂簸，以養其姑。

translations.literal: Within the jurisdiction was a woman who hired out her labor, spinning, weaving, pounding, and winnowing, to support her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction a woman hired out her labor—spinning, weaving, pounding, and winnowing—to support her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑感婦孝，每受食，即以手加額仰天而祝之。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law, moved by the daughter-in-law's filial piety, each time she received food would place her hand on her forehead and look up to Heaven in blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her daughter-in-law's devotion, the mother-in-law, each time she was fed, would press her hand to her forehead and look up to Heaven in prayer.

sentences.zh: 其子為人牧牛，亦幹飯以餉祖母。

translations.literal: Her son, herding cattle for others, also brought dry rice to feed his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Her son, while herding cattle for others, also brought dry rice to feed his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 迥廉得之，為紀其事，白於郡，郡給以錢粟。

translations.literal: Jiong learned of it through investigation, recorded the affair, reported to the prefecture, and the prefecture granted them money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong learned of the case through investigation, recorded it, and reported to the prefecture, which granted them money and grain.

sentences.zh: 調信州上饒縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shangrao County in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shangrao County in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲納租數萬石，舊法加倍，又取斛麵米。

translations.literal: Each year tens of thousands of piculs of rent were paid in; by the old method the amount was doubled, and in addition husked surface rice was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Each year tens of thousands of piculs of rent were collected. Under the old practice the amount was doubled, and husked surface rice was taken as well.

sentences.zh: 迥力止絕之，嚐曰：“令與吏服食者，皆此邦之民膏血也。

translations.literal: Jiong strove to stop and abolish this, once saying, "What magistrates and clerks eat and wear—all is the fat and blood of the people of this land.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong worked hard to abolish these exactions, saying once, "What magistrates and clerks eat and wear is the lifeblood of the people of this land.

sentences.zh: 曾不是思，而橫斂虐民，鬼神其無知乎！

translations.literal: Yet you never reflect on this, but levy harshly and tyrannize the people—do the spirits not know?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you never reflect on this, but levy harshly and oppress the people—do the spirits not see?

sentences.zh: ”州郡督索經總錢甚急，迥曰：“斯錢古之除陌之類，今其類乃三倍正賦，民何以堪？

translations.literal: " The prefecture and commandery pressed urgently for collection of the comprehensive transit levy; Jiong said, "This money is of the kind of the ancient chumo deduction; today its kind is triple the regular levy—how can the people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: " The prefecture pressed urgently for collection of the comprehensive transit levy. Jiong said, "This levy is like the ancient chumo surcharge, yet today it amounts to triple the regular tax—how can the people bear it?

sentences.zh: 反復言之當路。

translations.literal: He argued this repeatedly to those in power.
translations.idiomatic: He argued this point repeatedly to those in power.

sentences.zh: 奉祠，寓居番陽之蕭寺。

translations.literal: He received a temple appointment and lodged at a Buddhist monastery in Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving a temple stipend he lodged at a Buddhist monastery in Poyang.

sentences.zh: 程祥者，從伯父待制昌禹來居番陽，昌禹死，遂失所依。

translations.literal: There was one Cheng Xiang, whose father's elder brother, the Hanlin Attendant-Drafter Changyu, had come to live in Poyang; when Changyu died, Xiang lost his support.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Cheng Xiang had come to Poyang with his father's elder brother Changyu, a Hanlin Attendant-Drafter. When Changyu died, Xiang was left without support.

sentences.zh: 祥繼亡，祥妻度氏猶質賣奩具以撫育孤子，久之罄竭，瀕死，鄰家皆莫識其面。

translations.literal: Xiang also died; Xiang's wife, Lady Du, still pawned and sold her dowry to rear the orphaned son; after long years all was exhausted, and she was near death; the neighbors did not even know her face.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang also died. His wife Lady Du pawned and sold her dowry to raise their orphaned son. After years everything was gone and she was near death; her neighbors scarcely knew her by sight.

sentences.zh: 有欲醮之者，度曰：“吾兒幼，若事他人，使母不得撫其子，豈不負良人乎？

translations.literal: Someone wished to arrange a second marriage for her; Lady Du said, "My son is young; if I serve another man and a mother may not rear her own child, would I not fail my late husband?
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed remarriage for her, Lady Du said, "My son is still young. If I married another man, I could not raise my own child—would I not betray my late husband?

sentences.zh: ”終辭焉。

translations.literal: " In the end she declined.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused in the end.

sentences.zh: 或為迥言其事，迥走告於郡守，月給之錢粟。

translations.literal: Someone told Jiong of the affair; Jiong ran to inform the prefect, who granted her monthly money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When someone told Jiong of her plight, he hurried to inform the prefect, who granted her a monthly allowance of money and grain.

sentences.zh: 迥居官臨之以莊，政寬而明，令簡而信，綏強撫弱，導以恩義。

translations.literal: In office Jiong faced people with dignity; his government was lenient yet clear, his orders simple yet trustworthy; he pacified the strong and comforted the weak, guiding them with kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In office Jiong met people with dignified bearing. His administration was lenient yet clear, his orders simple yet trustworthy. He pacified the strong, comforted the weak, and guided all with kindness and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 積年讎訟，一語解去。

translations.literal: Litigation feuds of many years were dissolved with a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Feuds of many years' standing were settled with a single word from him.

sentences.zh: 猾吏奸民，皆以感激，久而悛悔，欺詐以革。

translations.literal: Crafty clerks and treacherous commoners were all moved to gratitude; in time they repented and reformed, and deceit was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty clerks and dishonest commoners were all moved by his example; in time they repented, and fraud was rooted out.

sentences.zh: 暇則賓禮賢士，從容盡歡，進其子弟之秀者與之均禮，為之陳說《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: In leisure he received worthy men as guests with ceremony, at ease enjoying full conviviality; he advanced their outstanding sons and nephews to equal courtesy with them, and for them expounded the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure he entertained worthy men as honored guests and enjoyed their company fully. He treated their most promising sons and nephews as equals and expounded the Odes and Documents for them.

sentences.zh: 質疑問難者，不問蚤暮。

translations.literal: Those who raised doubts and posed difficult questions—he did not ask whether it was early or late.
translations.idiomatic: He answered questions from students at any hour, early or late.

sentences.zh: 勢位不得以交私，祠廟非典祀不謁。

translations.literal: Rank and position could not be used to form private ties; he did not visit shrines and temples except for canonical sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no private favors on account of rank or position, and visited no shrine except for canonical state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 隱德潛善，無問幽明，皆表而出之，以勵風俗。

translations.literal: Hidden virtue and concealed good deeds, whether in obscurity or in the open, he all brought forth in memorials to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden virtue and quiet good deeds, whether known or unknown, he brought to light in memorials to encourage moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 或周其窮厄，俾全節行。

translations.literal: Sometimes he relieved their destitution so they could preserve their integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he relieved their poverty so they could preserve their integrity.

sentences.zh: 聽決獄訟，期於明允。

translations.literal: In hearing and deciding lawsuits, he aimed at clarity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In hearing lawsuits he aimed at clarity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 凡上官所未悉者，必再三抗辨，不為苟止。

translations.literal: Whenever superiors did not understand a matter, he invariably argued against them repeatedly and would not desist perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his superiors misunderstood a matter, he argued against them repeatedly and would not give way lightly.

sentences.zh: 貴溪民偽作吳漸名，誣訴縣令石邦彥，迥言匿名書不當受，轉運使不謂然，遂興大獄，瘐死者十有四人。

translations.literal: A resident of Guixi forged the name Wu Jian and falsely accused the county magistrate Shi Bangyan; Jiong said anonymous letters ought not to be accepted; the transport commissioner did not agree, and a great case was raised; fourteen died of mistreatment in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A man in Guixi forged the name Wu Jian and falsely accused the county magistrate Shi Bangyan. Jiong argued that anonymous accusations should not be accepted, but the transport commissioner disagreed and launched a major prosecution in which fourteen people died of mistreatment in custody.

sentences.zh: 及聞省寺，訖報如迥言。

translations.literal: When it reached the provincial offices, the final report accorded with what Jiong had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the provincial offices, the final ruling matched Jiong's argument.

sentences.zh: 迥嚐授經學於昆山王葆、嘉禾聞人茂德、嚴陵喻樗。

translations.literal: Jiong once received classical learning from Wang Bao of Kunshan, Wenren Maode of Jiahe, and Yu Chu of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had studied the classics under Wang Bao of Kunshan, Wenren Maode of Jiahe, and Yu Chu of Yanling.

sentences.zh: 所著有《古易考》、《古易章句》、《古占法》、《易傳外編》、《春秋傳顯微例目》、《論語傳》、《孟子章句》《文史評》、《經史說諸論辨》、《太玄補讚》、《戶口田製貢賦書》、《乾道振濟錄》、《醫經正本書》、《條具乾道新書》、《度量權三器圖義》、《四聲韻》、《淳熙雜志》、《南齋小集》。

translations.literal: His writings include Investigations into the Ancient Changes, Section-and-clause on the Ancient Changes, Ancient Methods of Divination, Supplementary Compilation to the Commentary on the Changes, Outline of Subtle Examples in the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Commentary on the Analects, Section-and-clause on Mencius, Literary and Historical Critique, Various Discussions and Debates on Classics and Histories, Supplementary Praise to the Supreme Mystery, Book on Household Registers, Field Systems, and Tribute and Levies, Record of Longxing Relief, Correct Text of the Medical Canon, Memorial Itemizing the Longxing New Books, Illustrated Meaning of the Three Measures, Weights, and Vessels, Rhymes of the Four Tones, Miscellaneous Records of the Chunxi Era, and Small Collection from the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Investigations into the Ancient Changes, Section-and-clause on the Ancient Changes, Ancient Methods of Divination, Supplementary Compilation to the Commentary on the Changes, Outline of Subtle Examples in the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Commentary on the Analects, Section-and-clause on Mencius, Literary and Historical Critique, Various Discussions and Debates on Classics and Histories, Supplementary Praise to the Supreme Mystery, Book on Household Registers, Field Systems, and Tribute and Levies, Record of Longxing Relief, Correct Text of the Medical Canon, Memorial Itemizing the Longxing New Books, Illustrated Meaning of the Three Measures, Weights, and Vessels, Rhymes of the Four Tones, Miscellaneous Records of the Chunxi Era, and Small Collection from the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 朝奉郎朱熹以書告迥子絢曰：“敬惟先德，博聞至行，追配古人，釋經訂史，開悟後學，當世之務又所通該，非獨章句之儒而已。

translations.literal: Court Gentleman Zhu Xi wrote to Jiong's son Xuan, saying, "I respectfully consider your late father's virtue: broad learning and consummate conduct, worthy to be paired with the ancients; he expounded the classics and revised histories, enlightened later students, and was also thoroughly versed in affairs of the age—not merely a classicist of section and clause.
translations.idiomatic: Court Gentleman Zhu Xi wrote to Jiong's son Xuan: "I deeply respect your late father's virtue—his broad learning and exemplary conduct worthy of the ancients, his exegesis of the classics and revision of historical texts, his enlightenment of later students, and his thorough grasp of affairs of the age. He was no mere commentator on individual passages.

sentences.zh: 曾不得一試，而奄棄盛時，此有誌之士所為悼歎谘嗟而不能已者。

translations.literal: Yet he never received a single trial of his talent, but suddenly left the flourishing age—this is what men of purpose lament, sigh over, and consult one another about without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was never given a full trial of his talents before he was suddenly taken in his prime—this is what men of purpose mourn and lament without end.

sentences.zh: 然著書滿家，足以傳世，是亦足以不朽。

translations.literal: Yet his writings fill the house, sufficient to pass down through generations—this too is enough for immortality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his writings fill the house and are enough to pass down through the ages—that alone is immortality enough.

sentences.zh: ”絢以致仕恩調巴陵尉，攝邑事，能理冤獄。

translations.literal: " Xuan, through his father's retirement privilege, was appointed marshal of Baling, acting in county affairs, and was able to settle wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan, through his father's retirement privilege, was appointed marshal of Baling, where he acted in county affairs and was able to clear wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 孫仲熊，亦有名。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhongxiong also had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhongxiong also won renown.

sentences.zh: 劉清之

translations.literal: Liu Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingzhi

sentences.zh: 劉清之，字子澄，臨江人，受業於兄靖之，甘貧力學，博極書傳。

translations.literal: Liu Qingzhi, courtesy name Zicheng, was a native of Linjiang; he received instruction from his elder brother Jingzhi, willingly endured poverty and studied with effort, and mastered the breadth of books and transmissions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingzhi, whose courtesy name was Zicheng, came from Linjiang. He studied under his elder brother Jingzhi, willingly endured poverty while pursuing learning, and mastered the breadth of the classical tradition.

sentences.zh: 登紹興二十七年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of the Shaoxing era (1157).

sentences.zh: 調袁州宜春縣主簿，未上，丁父憂，服除，改建德縣主簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of Yichun in Yuanzhou; before taking up the post he mourned his father's death; when mourning ended, he was reassigned as chief clerk of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Yichun in Yuanzhou, but before taking up the post he mourned his father's death. When the mourning period ended, he was reassigned as chief clerk of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 請於州，俾民自實其戶。

translations.literal: He requested of the prefecture that the people be allowed to report their own household registers truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the prefecture to let the people register their own households truthfully.

sentences.zh: 由是賦役平，爭訟息。

translations.literal: Thereby levies and corvée were equitable, and litigation ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As a result tax and corvée burdens were fair, and litigation died down.

sentences.zh: 調萬安縣丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 時江右大侵，郡檄視旱，徒步阡陌，親與民接，凡所蠲除，具得其實。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangyou suffered great famine; the prefecture issued orders to inspect the drought; he walked the fields on foot, personally meeting the people, and for all remissions he obtained the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiangyou suffered a severe famine. When the prefecture ordered drought inspection, he walked the fields on foot, met the people personally, and verified every remission on the ground.

sentences.zh: 州議減常平米直，清之曰：“此惠不過三十里內耳，外鄉遠民勢豈能來？

translations.literal: The prefecture deliberated reducing the market price of ever-normal granary rice; Qingzhi said, "This benefit extends no more than thirty li; how could distant commoners from outer townships come?
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture proposed lowering the price of ever-normal granary rice. Qingzhi objected, "That relief would reach no more than thirty li. How could people from distant townships come?

sentences.zh: 老幼疾患之人必有餒死者。

translations.literal: The old, the young, and the sick will surely have some who starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: The old, the young, and the sick would surely starve.

sentences.zh: 今有粟之家閉不肯糶，實窺伺攘奪者眾也。

translations.literal: Now households with grain shut their doors and refuse to sell; in truth many are watching for opportunities to seize by force.
translations.idiomatic: Now households with grain hoard it and refuse to sell, while many others watch for a chance to seize grain by force.

sentences.zh: 在我有政，則大家得錢，細民得米，兩適其便。

translations.literal: If we have proper government, then wealthy households obtain money and common people obtain rice—both get what suits them.
translations.idiomatic: With sound policy, wealthy households would get their money and common people their rice—both would benefit.

sentences.zh: ”乃請均境內之地為八，俾有粟者分振其鄉，官為主之。

translations.literal: " He then requested dividing the territory within the jurisdiction into eight parts, so that those with grain could distribute relief each in their own township, with the government presiding.
translations.idiomatic: " He then proposed dividing the jurisdiction into eight districts so that households with grain could distribute relief in their own townships under official supervision.

sentences.zh: 規畫防閑，民甚賴之。

translations.literal: He planned safeguards and precautions; the people relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He devised safeguards for the scheme, and the people relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 帥龔茂良以救荒實跡聞於朝，又偕諸公薦之。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Gong Maoliang reported his actual deeds in famine relief to the court, and together with several grandees recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Gong Maoliang reported Qingzhi's famine-relief work to the court, and together with other officials recommended him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 發運使史正誌按部至筠，俾清之拘集州縣畸零之賦，清之不可。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Shi Zhengzhi, on circuit inspection, reached Jun and ordered Qingzhi to round up and collect odd fractional levies from prefectures and counties; Qingzhi refused.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Shi Zhengzhi, on circuit inspection, reached Jun and ordered Qingzhi to round up odd fractional levies from prefectures and counties. Qingzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 清之有同年生在幕中，謂曰：“侍郎因子言，謂子愛民特立，將薦子矣，其以閥閱來。

translations.literal: Qingzhi had a fellow examination-year graduate in the commissioner's staff who said to him, "The Vice Minister, on account of your words, says you love the people and stand apart—he will recommend you; come with your pedigree of eminence."
translations.idiomatic: A fellow jinshi-year graduate on the commissioner's staff told him, "The Vice Minister, impressed by your stand, says he will recommend you—come present your pedigree of eminence."

sentences.zh: ”清之貽之以書曰：“所謂贏資者，皆州縣侵刻於民，法所當禁。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi sent him a letter, saying, "What is called surplus funds are all what prefectures and counties have extorted from the people—what the law ought to forbid.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingzhi wrote back: "What you call surplus funds is what prefectures and counties have extorted from the people—what the law forbids.

sentences.zh: 縱有贏資，是所謂羨餘也，獻之自下而詔止之，今則止而求之，乃自上焉。

translations.literal: Even if there were surplus funds, these are what are called excess remainders—presented from below and halted by imperial edict; now you halt and then demand them—from above.
translations.idiomatic: Even if surplus funds existed, they would be excess remainders properly presented from below and halted by imperial edict. Now you halt them and then demand them—from above.

sentences.zh: 不奪不饜，其弊有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: If you do not seize your fill, the abuses are beyond telling.
translations.idiomatic: If officials are never satisfied, the abuses are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 願侍郎自請於朝，姑歸貳卿之班，主大農經費，以佐國家。

translations.literal: I hope the Vice Minister will request of the court to return for a time to the ranks of the two vice ministers and oversee the great agricultural expenditures to assist the state.
translations.idiomatic: I urge the Vice Minister to petition the court to return to a vice-ministerial post and oversee state finances to serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 如此，則士孰不願出侍郎之門？

translations.literal: If so, which scholar would not wish to come from the Vice Minister's gate?
translations.idiomatic: Then which scholar would not wish to be your protégé?

sentences.zh: 不然，某誠不敢玷侍郎知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I truly dare not stain the Vice Minister's discernment in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I dare not accept a recommendation that would stain your judgment of men."

sentences.zh: ”以薦者兩有審察之命，清之竟不見丞相，詣吏部銓，得知宜黃縣。

translations.literal: " Because the recommenders twice received orders for scrutiny, Qingzhi in the end did not see the chief councilor but went to the Ministry of Personnel for appointment and was assigned as magistrate of Yihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Because both recommenders received orders for scrutiny, Qingzhi never called on the chief councilor but went directly to the Ministry of Personnel and was appointed magistrate of Yihuang.

sentences.zh: 茂良入為參知政事，與丞相周必大薦清之於孝宗。

translations.literal: Maoliang entered court as Vice Grand Councilor and, with Chief Councilor Zhou Bida, recommended Qingzhi to Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoliang entered court as Vice Grand Councilor, he and Chief Councilor Zhou Bida recommended Qingzhi to Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 召入對，首論：“民困兵驕，大臣退托，小臣苟偷。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he first argued: "The people are distressed, the troops arrogant; great ministers withdraw and rely on excuses, petty officials are careless and steal advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he began: "The people are distressed and the troops arrogant; great ministers withdraw behind excuses while petty officials grow careless and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 願陛下廣覽兼聽，並謀合智，清明安定，提要挈綱而力行之。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will broadly survey and listen to all sides, combine counsel and unite wisdom, be clear and tranquil, grasp the essentials and take hold of the main cords and carry them out with force.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to listen broadly, combine counsel, keep government clear and stable, grasp the essentials, and carry reform through with resolve.

sentences.zh: 古今未有俗不可變、弊不可革者，變而通之，亦在陛下方寸之間耳。

translations.literal: In past and present there has never been custom that cannot change or abuse that cannot be reformed; to change and adapt lies within Your Majesty's own mind alone.
translations.idiomatic: No custom is unchangeable and no abuse irreformable—to transform them lies within Your Majesty's own resolve."

sentences.zh: ”又言用人四事：“一曰辨賢否。

translations.literal: " He also spoke of four matters in employing men: "First, distinguish worthy from unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: " He also set forth four principles of appointment. First: distinguish the worthy from the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 謂道義之臣，大者可當經綸，小者可為儀刑。

translations.literal: By this is meant ministers of the Way and righteousness—the great may undertake statecraft, the small may serve as models of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Men of moral principle—the great may govern the realm, the lesser may serve as models of conduct.

sentences.zh: 功名之士，大者可使臨政，小者可使立事。

translations.literal: Men of merit and fame—the great may be set to govern, the small may be set to accomplish affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Men of achievement—the great may administer government, the lesser may carry out tasks.

sentences.zh: 至於專謀富貴利達而已者下也。

translations.literal: As for those who scheme only for wealth, honor, and advancement—these are the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Those who scheme only for wealth and advancement rank lowest.

sentences.zh: 二曰正名實。

translations.literal: Second, rectify names and realities.
translations.idiomatic: Second: rectify names and realities.

sentences.zh: 今百有司職守不明，非曠其官，則失之侵逼。

translations.literal: Now the duties of the hundred offices are unclear—either they neglect their posts, or they err by encroaching on others.
translations.idiomatic: Today the duties of the hundred offices are unclear—officials either neglect their posts or encroach on others' responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 願詔史官考究設官之本意，各指其合主何事，製旨親定，載之命書，依開寶中差諸州通判故事，使人人曉然知之而行賞罰焉。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the historiographers to investigate the original intent in establishing offices, specify for each what affairs it ought to oversee, have the imperial rescript personally fixed and recorded in the command book, following the precedent of the Kaibao era in assigning supervisory commissioners to the various prefectures, so that everyone understands clearly and rewards and punishments may be applied.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to order the historiographers to investigate the original intent behind each office, specify what each should oversee, have an imperial rescript recorded in the command book following the Kaibao precedent for assigning supervisory commissioners, so that all may understand their duties and rewards and punishments may be applied.

sentences.zh: 三曰使材能。

translations.literal: Third, employ talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Third: employ talent according to ability.

sentences.zh: 謂軍旅必武臣，錢穀必能吏，必臨之以忠信不欺之士，使兩人者皆得以效其所長。

translations.literal: By this is meant that military affairs must go to martial officials and revenue to capable clerks, and they must be overseen by men of loyalty, trustworthiness, and honesty, so that both may display their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs require martial officials and revenue requires capable administrators, each overseen by men of loyalty and integrity so that both may display their strengths.

sentences.zh: 四曰聽換授。

translations.literal: Fourth, permit transfer of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: permit transfer of appointment.

sentences.zh: 謂文武之官不可用違其才，然不當許之自列，宜令文武臣四品以上，各以性行材略及文武藝，每歲互舉堪充左右選者一人，於合入資格外，稍與優獎。

translations.literal: By this is meant that civil and military officials should not be used contrary to their talents, yet they ought not be allowed to nominate themselves; civil and military officials of the fourth rank and above should each year, on the basis of character, conduct, ability, and civil or military arts, mutually recommend one person fit for appointment near the throne, and beyond the proper qualification rank, grant slight preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials should not be used contrary to their talents, but they should not nominate themselves. Officials of the fourth rank and above should each year recommend one colleague fit for appointment near the throne, with slight preferential reward beyond normal qualification requirements."

sentences.zh: 改太常寺主簿。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，通判鄂州。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother's death; when mourning ended, he served as supervisory commissioner of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother's death he served as supervisory commissioner of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 鄂大軍所駐，兵籍多偽，清之白郡及諸司，請自通判廳始，俾偽者以實自言而正之。

translations.literal: Ezhou was where a great army was stationed; many military registers were fraudulent; Qingzhi reported to the prefecture and various offices, requesting to begin with the supervisory commissioner's office and let those falsely registered confess truthfully and be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: A great army was stationed at Ezhou, and many military registers were fraudulent. Qingzhi reported to the prefecture and various offices, asking to begin with his own office and let those falsely registered confess and be corrected.

sentences.zh: 州有民妻張以節死，嘉祐中，詔封旌德縣君，表其墓曰“烈女”，中更兵火，至是無知其墓者，清之與郡守羅願訪而祠之。

translations.literal: In the prefecture was a commoner's wife, Lady Zhang, who died preserving her chastity; in the Jiayou era an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Jingde County and marked her tomb "Stern Woman"; amid the fires of war no one knew her tomb's location; Qingzhi and the prefect Luo Yuan sought it out and established a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner's wife surnamed Zhang had died preserving her chastity. In the Jiayou era she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jingde County and her tomb was marked "Stern Woman." After the fires of war no one knew where the tomb lay. Qingzhi and Prefect Luo Yuan found it and established a shrine.

sentences.zh: 鄂俗計利而尚鬼，家貧子壯則出贅，習為當然，而尤謹奉大洪山之祠，病者不藥而聽於巫，死則不葬而畀諸火，清之皆諭止之。

translations.literal: The custom of Ezhou calculated profit and honored spirits; poor families with grown sons sent them out as sons-in-law, taking this as natural, and especially revered the shrine on Great Hong Mountain—when ill they took no medicine but obeyed shamans; when dead they did not bury but gave the body to fire; Qingzhi admonished and stopped all this.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ezhou were profit-minded and superstitious. Poor families with grown sons sent them out as sons-in-law, taking this as natural. They especially revered the shrine on Great Hong Mountain: the sick took no medicine but obeyed shamans; the dead were not buried but cremated. Qingzhi admonished the people and put a stop to these practices.

sentences.zh: 差權發遣常州，改衡州。

translations.literal: He was assigned on temporary authority to dispatch Changzhou and was reassigned to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned on temporary authority to administer Changzhou and was then reassigned to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 衡自建炎軍興，有所請大軍月樁過湖錢者，歲送漕司，無慮七八萬緡，以四邑所入曲引錢及郡計畸零苗米折納充之。

translations.literal: Since the military rise of Jianyan, Heng had a requested levy called the great army's monthly pile and lake-crossing money, sent yearly to the transport office, no less than seventy or eighty thousand strings of cash, supplied from the four districts' quyin money and the prefecture's odd fractional rice converted to payment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jianyan military campaigns, Heng had owed an annual levy called the great army's monthly pile and lake-crossing money—some seventy or eighty thousand strings of cash sent to the transport office—paid from quyin money collected in four districts and odd fractional rice converted to payment.

sentences.zh: 舊法，民有吉凶聚會，許買引為酒曲，謂之曲引錢，其後直以等第敷納。

translations.literal: By the old law, when the people had gatherings for joy or sorrow they were permitted to buy permits for brewing yeast, called quyin money; later it was levied directly by household rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, when people held gatherings for weddings or funerals they could buy permits to brew yeast, called quyin money. Later the levy was imposed directly by household rank.

sentences.zh: 衡有五邑，獨敷其四。

translations.literal: Heng had five districts but levied only four.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had five districts but levied only four.

sentences.zh: 取民之辭不正，良民遍受其害，而黠民往往侮易其上，乃並與常賦不輸。

translations.literal: The grounds for taking from the people were not upright; good commoners suffered harm throughout, while crafty commoners often treated their superiors with contempt and together with the regular levies paid nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The levy lacked legitimate grounds. Honest commoners suffered throughout, while crafty ones often defied their superiors and refused to pay even regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 雖得曲引錢四五萬緡，而常賦之失，不啻數萬緡矣。

translations.literal: Although forty or fifty thousand strings of quyin money were obtained, the loss in regular levies was no less than tens of thousands of strings.
translations.idiomatic: Although forty or fifty thousand strings of quyin money were collected, the loss in regular levies amounted to tens of thousands more.

sentences.zh: 清之請於朝，願與總領所酌損補移，漸圖蠲減。

translations.literal: Qingzhi petitioned the court, wishing to consult with the general supervisory office on reductions and transfers and gradually seek remission.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi petitioned the court to consult with the general supervisory office on reductions and gradually seek remission.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came.

sentences.zh: 遂戒諸邑：董常賦，緩雜征，閣舊逋，戒預折，新簿籍，謹推收，督勾銷，明逋負，防帶鈔，治頑梗，柅吏奸，擾戶長，費用有節，滲漏有防，稽考有政，補置有漸。

translations.literal: He then admonished all districts: supervise regular levies, ease miscellaneous exactions, suspend old arrears, forbid advance conversion, renew registers, carefully pursue collection, supervise verification and cancellation, clarify outstanding debts, guard against carrying over notes, deal with the stubborn, restrain clerical corruption, stop harassing household heads, keep expenditures within bounds, guard against leakage, conduct audits with discipline, and make replacements gradually.
translations.idiomatic: He then instructed all districts: supervise regular levies, ease miscellaneous exactions, suspend old arrears, forbid advance conversion, renew registers, pursue collection carefully, supervise verification, clarify outstanding debts, guard against carrying over notes, deal with the stubborn, restrain clerical corruption, stop harassing household heads, keep expenditures within bounds, guard against leakage, conduct disciplined audits, and make replacements gradually.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡飾廚傳以事常平、刑獄二使者，月一會集，互致折饋。

translations.literal: Previously the prefecture had adorned its kitchens and lodges to entertain the two commissioners of the Ever-Normal Granary and Penal Affairs, meeting monthly and exchanging gifts of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefecture had lavishly entertained the commissioners of the Ever-Normal Granary and Penal Affairs, meeting monthly and exchanging gifts.

sentences.zh: 清之歎曰：“此何時也？

translations.literal: Qingzhi sighed and said, "What time is this?
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sighed and said, "What times are these?

sentences.zh: 與其取諸民，孰若裁諸公。

translations.literal: Rather than take from the people, how much better to cut from public funds.
translations.idiomatic: Better to cut public expenditures than to take from the people.

sentences.zh: 吾之所以事上官者，惟究心於所職，無負於吾民足矣。

translations.literal: What I use to serve superiors is only to devote my heart to my duties and not fail my people—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: What I owe my superiors is devotion to my duties and not failing my people—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 豈以酒食貨財為勤哉？

translations.literal: How could wine, food, and wealth be called diligence?
translations.idiomatic: How could wine, food, and gifts count as diligence?

sentences.zh: ”清之自常祿外，悉歸之公帑，以佐經用。

translations.literal: " Beyond his regular salary Qingzhi turned everything over to the public treasury to assist regular expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: " Beyond his regular salary Qingzhi turned everything over to the public treasury to assist regular expenditures.

sentences.zh: 至之日，兵無糧，官無奉，上供送使無可備。

translations.literal: On the day he arrived, the troops had no grain, officials had no salaries, and nothing could be prepared for tribute and dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the troops had no grain, officials had no salaries, and nothing could be prepared for tribute payments or dispatch envoys.

sentences.zh: 已而郡計漸裕。

translations.literal: Before long the prefectural accounts grew ample.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the prefectural treasury grew ample.

sentences.zh: 民力稍蘇。

translations.literal: The people's strength revived somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The people's burdens eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 或有報白，手自書之，吏不與焉。

translations.literal: When there were reports he wrote them with his own hand; clerks were not involved.
translations.idiomatic: When reports arrived he wrote them out himself without involving clerks.

sentences.zh: 嚐作《諭民書》一編，首言畏天積善，勤力務本，農工商賈莫不有勸，教以事親睦族，教子祀先，謹身節用，利物濟人，婚姻以時，喪葬以禮。

translations.literal: He once composed a book Admonishing the People in one fascicle, opening with revering Heaven and accumulating goodness, working diligently and attending to fundamentals, with encouragement for farmers, craftsmen, merchants, and traders alike, teaching filial service to parents and harmony in the clan, instructing sons and sacrificing to ancestors, keeping the person restrained and expenditures frugal, benefiting things and aiding people, marrying at the proper season, and burying according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a book Admonishing the People, opening with reverence for Heaven and accumulation of virtue, urging diligence and attention to fundamentals, with encouragement for farmers, craftsmen, merchants, and traders alike. He taught filial devotion to parents, harmony within the clan, instruction of sons and sacrifice to ancestors, personal restraint and frugality, benefiting others, timely marriage, and burial according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 詞意質直，簡而易從。

translations.literal: The wording was plain and direct, simple and easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The language was plain and direct, simple and easy to follow.

sentences.zh: 邦人家有其書，非理之訟日為衰息。

translations.literal: Every household in the prefecture had the book; unreasonable lawsuits daily declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Every household in the prefecture possessed a copy, and unreasonable lawsuits daily declined.

sentences.zh: 念士風未振，每因月講，復具酒肴以燕諸生，相與輸情論學，設為疑問，以觀其所向，然後從容示以先後本末之序。

translations.literal: Mindful that scholarly custom was not yet revived, at each monthly lecture he again prepared wine and dishes to feast the students, exchanging sentiments and discussing learning together, posing difficult questions to observe their inclinations, then calmly showing them the order of first and last, root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that scholarly culture had not yet revived, at each monthly lecture he prepared wine and food to feast the students, exchanging views and discussing learning. He posed difficult questions to observe their inclinations, then calmly showed them the proper order of study from fundamentals to applications.

sentences.zh: 來者日眾，則增築臨蒸精舍居之。

translations.literal: As those who came grew daily more numerous, he enlarged and built the Linying Hermitage to house them.
translations.idiomatic: As students grew in number he enlarged and built the Linying Hermitage to house them.

sentences.zh: 其所講，先正經，次訓詁音釋，次疏先儒議論，次述今所繹之說，然後各指其所宜用，人君治天下，諸侯治一國，學者治心治身治家治人，確然皆有可舉而措之之實。

translations.literal: What he lectured on: first the canonical classics, next exegesis and phonetic glosses, next commentaries on former Confucians' discussions, next setting forth today's interpretive doctrines, then indicating for each what ought to be applied—the ruler governing all under Heaven, the feudal lord governing one state, the scholar governing the mind, the person, the family, and others—with solid realities that could be lifted up and set in place.
translations.idiomatic: His lectures proceeded from the canonical classics to exegesis and phonetic glosses, then to commentaries on former Confucians, then to his own interpretations, and finally to practical application—how the ruler governs the realm, how the feudal lord governs a state, how the scholar governs mind, person, family, and community—with concrete principles that could be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 為閱武場。

translations.literal: He established a drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: He established a drill ground.

sentences.zh: 凡禁軍役於他所，隱於百工者，悉按軍籍俾詣訓閱。

translations.literal: All forbidden troops serving elsewhere who hid among the hundred crafts—he checked the military registers and ordered them to come for training and review.
translations.idiomatic: All forbidden troops serving elsewhere who had hidden among civilian trades were checked against the military registers and ordered to report for training and review.

sentences.zh: 作朱陵道院，祠張九齡、韓愈、寇準、周敦頤、胡安國於左，祠晉死節太守劉翼、宋死節內史王應之於右。

translations.literal: He built the Zhuling Daoist Abbey, enshrining on the left Zhang Jiuling, Han Yu, Kou Zhun, Zhou Dunyi, and Hu Anguo, and on the right the Jin martyr Prefect Liu Yi and the Song martyr Palace Secretary Wang Yingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Zhuling Daoist Abbey, enshrining on the left Zhang Jiuling, Han Yu, Kou Zhun, Zhou Dunyi, and Hu Anguo, and on the right the Jin martyr Prefect Liu Yi and the Song martyr Palace Secretary Wang Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 雅儒吉士日相周旋其間，而參佐謀論多在焉。

translations.literal: Refined Confucians and worthy gentlemen daily mingled there, and most policy deliberations among aides took place there.
translations.idiomatic: Refined scholars and worthy gentlemen gathered there daily, and most policy deliberations among his staff took place there.

sentences.zh: 劉孝昌者，摯之孫也，貧不自立，清之買田以給之。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaochang was the grandson of Zhi; poor and unable to support himself, Qingzhi bought land to provide for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaochang, grandson of Zhi, was too poor to support himself; Qingzhi bought land to provide for him.

sentences.zh: 部使者以清之不能媚己，惡之，貽書所厚台臣，誣以勞民用財，論罷，主管雲台觀。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner, because Qingzhi could not flatter him, hated him and sent a letter to a censor he favored, falsely accusing him of wasting the people's labor and wealth; he was dismissed from office and appointed to supervise the Yuntai Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner, resenting Qingzhi's refusal to flatter him, wrote to a favored censor falsely accusing him of wasting public funds on the people. Qingzhi was dismissed and appointed to supervise the Yuntai Abbey.

sentences.zh: 初，清之既舉進士，欲應博學宏詞科。

translations.literal: At first, after Qingzhi had passed the jinshi examination, he wished to compete in the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, Qingzhi had wished to compete in the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination.

sentences.zh: 及見朱熹，盡取所習焚之，慨然誌於義理之學。

translations.literal: When he met Zhu Xi he took all he had studied and burned it, and with deep feeling set his will on the learning of principle and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Zhu Xi he burned all he had studied and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the learning of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 呂伯恭、張栻皆神交心契，汪應辰、李燾亦敬慕之。

translations.literal: Lü Zuqian and Zhang Shi were both spiritual friends of matching hearts; Wang Yingchen and Li Tao also admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuqian and Zhang Shi were spiritual friends of matching hearts; Wang Yingchen and Li Tao also admired him.

sentences.zh: 母不逮養，每展閱手澤，涕泗交頤。

translations.literal: His mother he could not serve in life; each time he unrolled and read her surviving handwriting, tears and mucus streamed down his cheeks.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to serve his mother in her lifetime, he wept whenever he read her surviving handwriting.

sentences.zh: 從兄肅流落新吳，族父曄寓丹陽、艾寓臨川，皆迎養之。

translations.literal: His cousin Su, adrift in Xinwu; his clan uncle Ye, lodging in Danyang; and Ai, lodging in Linchuan—all he received and supported.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Su, adrift in Xinwu; his clan uncles Ye in Danyang and Ai in Linchuan—he received and supported them all.

sentences.zh: 從祖子僑為邵州錄事參軍，死吳錫之亂，清之遣其孫晉之致書邵守，得其遺骨歸葬焉。

translations.literal: His collateral ancestor Ziqiao had been recorder of Shaozhou and died in the disorder of Wu Xi; Qingzhi sent his grandson Jinzhi to write the prefect of Shao and obtained his remains to return and bury.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral ancestor Ziqiao, recorder of Shaozhou, had died in the disorder of Wu Xi. Qingzhi sent his grandson Jinzhi to write the prefect of Shao and recovered his remains for burial.

sentences.zh: 族人自遠來，館留之，不忍使之遽去。

translations.literal: When clansmen came from afar he lodged and kept them, unwilling to let them depart hastily.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen came from afar he lodged them and was reluctant to let them leave quickly.

sentences.zh: 嚐序範仲淹《義莊規矩》，勸大家族眾者隨力行之。

translations.literal: He once arranged Fan Zhongyan's Rules of the Charity Estate and urged large clans with many members to carry them out according to their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged Fan Zhongyan's Rules of the Charity Estate and urged large clans to implement them according to their means.

sentences.zh: 本之家法，參取先儒禮書，定為祭禮行之。

translations.literal: Based on his family's rules, drawing on former Confucians' ritual books, he fixed sacrificial rites and carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on his family's rules and former Confucians' ritual books, he established sacrificial rites and carried them out.

sentences.zh: 高安李好古以族人有以財為訟，見清之豫章，清之為說《訟》、《家人》二卦，好古惕然，遽舍所訟，市程氏《易》以歸，卒為善士。

translations.literal: Li Haogu of Gao'an, because a clansman was suing over property, met Qingzhi in Yuzhang; Qingzhi expounded for him the hexagrams Litigation and Family; Haogu was startled into vigilance, hastily abandoned the suit, bought the Cheng clan's Changes and returned home, and in the end became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haogu of Gao'an met Qingzhi in Yuzhang while suing a clansman over property. Qingzhi expounded the hexagrams Litigation and Family for him. Startled into reflection, Haogu abandoned the suit, bought the Cheng clan's Changes, and in the end became a good man.

sentences.zh: 所著有《曾子內外雜篇》、《訓蒙新書外書》、《戒子通錄》、《墨莊總錄》、《祭儀》、《時令書》、《續說苑》、文集、《農書》。

translations.literal: His writings include the Inner and Outer Miscellaneous Chapters of Zengzi, Outer Book of the New Book for Instruction of the Young, General Record for Admonishing Sons, General Record of the Ink Estate, Sacrificial Rites, Book of Seasons, Continued Garden of Persuasions, collected writings, and Book of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Inner and Outer Miscellaneous Chapters of Zengzi, Outer Book of the New Book for Instruction of the Young, General Record for Admonishing Sons, General Record of the Ink Estate, Sacrificial Rites, Book of Seasons, Continued Garden of Persuasions, collected writings, and Book of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 真德秀

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu

sentences.zh: 真德秀，字景元，後更為希元，建之浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu, courtesy name Jingyuan, later changed to Xiyuan, was a native of Pucheng in Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan and who later changed it to Xiyuan, came from Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四歲受書，過目成誦。

translations.literal: At four he received books; what passed before his eyes he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: At four he began to study; what he read once he could recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 十五而孤，母吳氏力貧教之。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was orphaned; his mother, Lady Wu, strained in poverty to teach him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fifteen, he was raised in poverty by his mother, Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 同郡楊圭見而異之，使歸共諸子學，卒妻以女。

translations.literal: Yang Gui of the same commandery, seeing him and finding him extraordinary, had him return to study with his sons, and in the end gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui of the same commandery, struck by his talent, had him study with his sons and eventually gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 登慶元五年進士第，授南劍州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Qingyuan and was appointed judge of Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Qingyuan era (1199) and was appointed judge of Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 繼試，中博學宏詞科，入閩帥幕，召為太學正，嘉定元年遷博士。

translations.literal: He then competed again, passed the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination, entered the Fujian commander's staff, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Academy, and in the first year of Jiading was promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination, entered the Fujian commander's staff, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Academy, and in the first year of Jiading (1208) was promoted to Erudite.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄已誅，入對，首言：“權臣開邊，南北塗炭，今茲繼好，豈非天下之福？

translations.literal: At the time Han Tuozhou had already been executed; entering audience, he first said: "The powerful minister opened the frontier; north and south were scorched; now renewing good relations—is this not the fortune of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou had already been executed. In his first audience Dexiu said: "The powerful minister opened hostilities and north and south were laid waste. Now that good relations are renewed, is this not the fortune of the realm?

sentences.zh: 然日者以行人之遣，金人欲多歲幣之數，而吾亦曰可增；

translations.literal: Yet recently, on the dispatch of envoys, the Jurchens wished to increase the annual tribute, and we also said it could be increased;
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently, when envoys were dispatched, the Jurchens demanded an increase in annual tribute, and we agreed;

sentences.zh: 金人欲得奸臣之首，而吾亦曰可與。

translations.literal: the Jurchens wished to obtain the head of the treacherous minister, and we also said it could be given.
translations.idiomatic: the Jurchens demanded the head of the treacherous minister, and we agreed to give it.

sentences.zh: 往來之稱謂，犒軍之金帛，根括歸明流徙之民，皆承之唯謹，得無滋嫚我乎？

translations.literal: Terms used in exchanges, gold and silk to reward troops, rounding up people who had fled to the Ming— all were accepted with sole scrupulousness; will this not increase their contempt for us?
translations.idiomatic: Terms of address in diplomatic exchanges, gold and silk to reward their troops, rounding up refugees who had fled to the Song—all were accepted without question. Will this not only increase their contempt for us?

sentences.zh: 抑善謀國者不觀敵情，觀吾政事。

translations.literal: Yet those skilled in planning for the state do not look at the enemy's situation—they look at our government and affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those skilled in statecraft do not look to the enemy's situation but to our own government.

sentences.zh: 今號為更化，而無以使敵情之畏服，正恐彼資吾歲賂以厚其力，乘吾不備以長其謀，一旦挑爭端而吾無以應，此有識所為寒心。

translations.literal: Now we are called reforming, yet have no means to make the enemy situation submit in awe; I truly fear they will use our annual payments to strengthen their power, seize our unpreparedness to extend their schemes, and one day provoke conflict while we have no means to respond—this is what men of insight find chilling.
translations.idiomatic: We call this an era of reform, yet we give the enemy no reason to respect us. I fear they will use our annual payments to strengthen themselves, exploit our unpreparedness to advance their schemes, and one day provoke conflict while we cannot respond. This is what men of insight find chilling."

sentences.zh: ”又言：“侂胄自知不為清議所貸，至誠憂國之士則名以好異，於是忠良之士斥，而正論不聞，正心誠意之學則誣以好名，於是偽學之論興，而正道不行。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Tuozhou knew he was not trusted by pure opinion; sincere men who truly cared for the state were labeled heterodox; thus loyal and good men were expelled and upright discourse was not heard; the learning of rectifying the mind and making intentions sincere was slandered as fondness for fame; thus the theory of false learning arose and the correct Way did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "Tuozhou knew he was not trusted by public opinion. Sincere patriots were labeled heterodox, loyal men were expelled, and upright discourse was silenced. The learning of rectifying the mind was slandered as mere love of fame, the charge of false learning arose, and the correct Way was blocked.

sentences.zh: 今日改弦更張，正當褒崇名節，明示好尚。

translations.literal: Today, in changing the strings and stretching the bow anew, it is precisely fitting to honor and exalt integrity of name and clearly display what is to be valued.
translations.idiomatic: Today, in this era of reform, we ought to honor integrity and clearly display what the court values."

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，改秘書省正字兼檢討玉牒。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy and was reassigned as proofreader of the Secretariat, concurrently collating the imperial genealogical record.
translations.idiomatic: He was examined at the Hanlin Academy and appointed proofreader of the Secretariat, concurrently collating the imperial genealogical record.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to collator.

sentences.zh: 又對，言暴風、雨雹、熒惑、蝻蝗之變，皆贓吏所致。

translations.literal: He again had audience and spoke of changes in violent winds, hail, the Sparkling Deluder, and locust larvae—all caused by corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In another audience he argued that violent winds, hail, the Sparkling Deluder, and locust plagues were all caused by corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 尋兼沂王府教授、學士院權直。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently instructor of the Prince of Yi's establishment and acting duty officer of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was concurrently instructor of the Prince of Yi's establishment and acting duty officer of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 入對，乞開公道，窒旁蹊，以抑小人道長之漸；

translations.literal: Entering audience, he begged to open the path of public justice, block side paths, and check the gradual advance of petty men's ways;
translations.idiomatic: In audience he urged the emperor to open the path of public justice, block side paths, and check the gradual rise of petty men;

sentences.zh: 選良牧，勵戰士，以扼群盜方張之銳。

translations.literal: select good prefects, encourage fighting troops, and contain the sharp advance of bandit hosts now spreading.
translations.idiomatic: select good prefects, encourage fighting troops, and contain the growing power of bandit armies.

sentences.zh: 四年，選著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was selected as assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was selected as assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 同列相惎讒之，德秀恬不與較。

translations.literal: Colleagues envied and slandered him; Dexiu was calm and did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues envied and slandered him; Dexiu remained calm and did not contend.

sentences.zh: 宰相將用德秀，會言官牴之，德秀力辭。

translations.literal: The chief councilor was about to employ Dexiu; censors happened to oppose it, and Dexiu forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor was about to appoint Dexiu, but censors opposed it and Dexiu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 兼禮部郎官，上疏言：“金有必亡之勢，亦可為中國憂。

translations.literal: Concurrently as a director in the Ministry of Rites, he submitted a memorial, saying: "Jin has the momentum of certain destruction, yet this may also be a worry for China.
translations.idiomatic: As a director in the Ministry of Rites he submitted a memorial: "Jin is headed for certain destruction, yet this may also worry China.

sentences.zh: 蓋金亡則上恬下嬉，憂不在敵而在我，多事之端恐自此始。

translations.literal: For when Jin perishes, those above grow complacent and those below grow playful; the worry is not in the enemy but in ourselves—the beginnings of many troubles may start from this.
translations.idiomatic: For when Jin falls, those above grow complacent and those below grow careless. The danger lies not in the enemy but in ourselves—the beginnings of many troubles may start here."

sentences.zh: ”五年，遷軍器少監，升權直。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Military Equipment and promoted to acting duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Military Equipment and promoted to acting duty officer.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷起居舍人，奏：“權奸擅政十有四年，朱熹、彭龜年以抗論逐，呂祖儉、周端朝以上書斥，當時近臣猶有爭之者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Diarist and memorialized: "The powerful traitor monopolized government for fourteen years; Zhu Xi and Peng Guinian were expelled for opposing him, Lü Zujian and Zhou Duanchao were cast out for submitting memorials—at the time close attendants still had some who contended with this.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Diarist and memorialized: "The powerful traitor monopolized government for fourteen years. Zhu Xi and Peng Guinian were expelled for opposing him; Lü Zujian and Zhou Duanchao were cast out for submitting memorials. At the time, some close attendants still spoke against this.

sentences.zh: 其後呂祖泰之貶，非惟近臣莫敢言，而台諫且出力以擠之，則嘉泰之失已深於慶元矣。

translations.literal: After that, Lü Zutai's demotion—not only did close attendants dare not speak, but censorial officials even exerted themselves to squeeze him out—then the failings of Jiatai were already deeper than those of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Zutai was demoted, not only did close attendants dare not speak, but censorial officials actively worked to suppress him. The failings of the Jiatai era were already worse than those of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 更化之初，群賢皆得自奮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reform, worthy men were all able to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reform, worthy men were all able to exert themselves.

sentences.zh: 未幾，傅伯成以諫官論事去，蔡幼學以詞臣論事去，鄒應龍、許奕又繼以封駁論事去。

translations.literal: Before long, Fu Bocheng left office for remonstrating as remonstrance official, Cai Youxue left as literary attendant, and Zou Yinglong and Xu Yi followed by leaving for sealed rebuttals.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Fu Bocheng left office after remonstrating as a remonstrance official, Cai Youxue left after remonstrating as a literary attendant, and Zou Yinglong and Xu Yi followed by leaving after sealed rebuttals.

sentences.zh: 是數人者，非能大有所矯拂，已皆不容於朝。

translations.literal: These several men—though unable to make great corrections—were already all intolerable at court.
translations.idiomatic: These men had not attempted great reforms, yet they were already intolerable at court.

sentences.zh: 故人務自全，一辭不措。

translations.literal: Thus men strove to preserve themselves and would not utter a word.
translations.idiomatic: Thus men strove only to preserve themselves and would not speak at all.

sentences.zh: 設有大安危、大利害，群臣喑嘿如此，豈不殆哉！

translations.literal: If there were great safety or danger, great benefit or harm, yet the ministers were dumb and silent like this—would it not be perilous!
translations.idiomatic: If great matters of safety or danger, benefit or harm arose, and the ministers remained as mute as this, would it not be perilous!

sentences.zh: 今欲與陛下言，勤訪問、廣謀議、明黜陟三者而已。

translations.literal: What I wish to speak to Your Majesty about is only three things: diligent inquiry, broad counsel and debate, and clear promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: What I wish to say to Your Majesty is only this: diligent inquiry, broad counsel and debate, and clear promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: ”時鈔法楮令行，告訐繁興，抵罪者眾，莫敢以上聞。

translations.literal: " At the time paper-money laws were enforced, denunciations flourished, many were punished, and none dared report upward.
translations.idiomatic: At that time paper-money laws were strictly enforced, denunciations flourished, many were punished, and none dared report upward.

sentences.zh: 德秀奏：“或一夫坐罪，而並籍昆弟之財；

translations.literal: Dexiu memorialized: "Sometimes one man was guilty, yet the property of brothers was all registered and confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu memorialized: "Sometimes one man was guilty, yet the property of his brothers was all registered and confiscated;

sentences.zh: 或虧陌四錢，而沒入百萬之貲。

translations.literal: sometimes a shortfall of four cash in changing money led to confiscation of property worth a million.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes a shortfall of four cash in changing money led to the confiscation of property worth a million.

sentences.zh: 至於科富室之錢，拘鹽商之舟，視產高下，配民藏楮，鬻田宅以收券者，雖大家不能免，尚得名便民之策？

translations.literal: As for levying money on wealthy households, detaining salt merchants' boats, assigning people to hoard paper notes according to wealth, and selling fields and houses to collect notes—even great families could not escape—can this still be called a policy that benefits the people?
translations.idiomatic: As for levying money on wealthy households, detaining salt merchants' boats, assigning people to hoard paper notes according to their wealth, and selling fields and houses to collect notes—even great families could not escape. Can this still be called a policy that benefits the people?

sentences.zh: ”自此籍沒之產以漸給還。

translations.literal: " From this, confiscated property was gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: From this point, confiscated property was gradually returned.

sentences.zh: 兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又言金人必亡，君臣上下皆當以祈天永命為心。

translations.literal: He also said the Jurchens would certainly perish, and ruler and subject above and below ought all to take praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate as their mind.
